hints: Notice that X and Z are the turning points of the swing while Y is the bottom centre - where is the speed zero and where is it maximum?
Recall the Doppler effect for sound: motion of the source towards a stationary observer compresses wavefronts and raises observed frequency, while motion away lowers it.
Combine maximum speed at Y with direction: compare moving towards the man versus moving away to decide which gives the highest observed frequency.
walkthrough: Identify the source and observer: the whistle is a moving source of constant frequency $f_s$ and the man is a stationary observer.
State the Doppler rule: observed frequency $f_o$ is higher than $f_s$ when the source has a velocity component towards the observer, and lower when the component is away.
Compare speeds: at the extremes X and Z the swing momentarily stops, so velocity is zero and $f_o = f_s$ with no shift.
At the bottom position Y the kinetic energy and speed are maximum, so the magnitude of the Doppler shift is largest there.
Add direction: moving towards the man at Y compresses the wavelength in front of the source, so $f_o > f_s$ and is a maximum, while moving away stretches it so $f_o < f_s$.

options.A: Position X is an extreme of the swing where the child momentarily stops, so the source speed towards the man is zero and there is no Doppler shift.
options.B: At Y the speed is maximum but moving away from the man stretches the waves, so the observed frequency is decreased to its lowest value.
options.C: At Y the speed is maximum and motion towards the man compresses the waves, giving the largest increase in observed frequency.
options.D: Position Z is the far extreme where the child momentarily stops, so the source speed along the line to the man is zero and there is no Doppler shift.
